narrative_summary: Recent developments reveal systemic vulnerabilities at the intersection of corporate power, national security, and political influence, highlighted by corporate governance crises at firms like Nvidia and ongoing debates over foreign policy illusions regarding China and Russia. Simultaneously, political landscapes shift dramatically as Democratic majorities in the 2026 midterms alter the legislative balance, while institutional and legal authorities face mounting pressure from judicial reexaminations and executive overreach. Across technology, climate, and public discourse, systems are straining under rapid transformation, from escalating atmospheric turbulence and energy policy gridlocks at COP31 to the societal impacts of digital integration on youth development.

source_summaries.title: Psychologist Sees Alarming Signs of Trump’s Decline (w/ John Gartner)
bullets: Clinical psychologist John Gartner and George Conway analyzed Donald Trump's behavior in relation to narcissistic and antisocial personality disorder criteria.
Gartner argued that a wounded narcissist may become increasingly dangerous as he loses power.
The discussion highlighted concerns regarding the risks of Trump's psychological profile and his authority over nuclear weapons.

source_summaries.title: Andrew Weissmann Explains Why Trump Can’t Pardon His Way Out of Everything
bullets: Democrats can utilize civil contempt to enforce congressional subpoenas and hold Trump administration officials accountable despite presidential pardons.
Legal tools are already available for Democrats to investigate administration corruption if they choose to use them.
Recent controversies involve questions surrounding Elise Stefanik's home sale and Trump's influence on Nvidia's corporate decisions regarding chip sales to China.

bullets: Right-wing figure Laura Loomer is utilizing her White House connections to target and advocate for the deportation of rival conservative influencers.
A rising MAGA personality has been linked to troubling ties with Russian intelligence operatives.
A Trump staffer inadvertently exposed internal plans regarding the restructuring of the Smithsonian Institution.

bullets: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO following input from U.S. government officials who determined he poses no national security risk.
President Donald Trump's recent Asia trip yielded no major policy wins or diplomatic advances while featuring praise for foreign dictators.
During a ninety-minute White House press conference, an unenthusiastic Trump made dubious claims about the economy and the midterm election results.

source_summaries.title: What does permitting reform have to do with housing?
bullets: The Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act in a 62-33 vote.
The legislation has been primarily debated in terms of energy and climate policy.
The bill's permitting reform provisions implicate a broad range of different kinds of construction projects.

He shares personal advice on dating and maintaining friendships.

source_summaries.title: Did the AI Bubble Just Pop?
bullets: Nvidia's stock has dropped significantly and faced leadership turmoil following CEO Jensen Huang's ousting and a subsequent SEC investigation into accounting issues.
Despite management changes and an impending shift toward more disciplined investments, Nvidia continues to report record earnings and strong revenue growth.
Anthropic launched the largest IPO in history, raising massive capital before giving up a significant portion of its initial gains within two days.

source_summaries.title: The Second Amendment and an "unusually dangerous" approach to dicta
bullets: A recent New York Times article argued that Justice Antonin Scalia's 2008 Heller opinion altered Second Amendment jurisprudence by misquoting William Blackstone's phrasing from "dangerous or unusual" to "dangerous and unusual."

While critics and defenders debate the significance of Scalia's historical citation, the true issue concerns how unbinding judicial dicta was subsequently transformed into a rigid legal test by later justices.
Judicial dicta lacks precedential authority because statements made in passing are not thoroughly investigated for their broad application to future cases.

source_summaries.title: Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson and the arc of the law
bullets: Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson views her dissents as an expression of faith in the future and a tool to bend the law toward justice.
Jackson has established a unique role within the Supreme Court's liberal bloc since joining the bench in 2022.
She frequently uses her opinions to offer an alternative vision and speak directly to the public, sometimes without the backing of fellow liberals.

source_summaries.title: The Supreme Court and profanity
bullets: In 1973, radio station WBAI broadcast George Carlin's satirical "Filthy Words" routine during an afternoon program about language.
A listener filed a complaint with the FCC, leading the commission to rule the broadcast indecent due to the risk of children listening.
The FCC's ruling was appealed to the Supreme Court after a federal appeals court set the order aside.

source_summaries.title: Justice Sotomayor addresses Supreme Court term limits
bullets: The Supreme Court building will be closed on Thursday and Friday for Thanksgiving.
The December argument session begins on Monday, November 30.
The court will hear arguments regarding the constitutionality of AR-15 bans in Viramontes v. Cook County on December 2.

source_summaries.title: Elon Musk Wants to Rewrite History. Here's What the Facts Say.
bullets: Fact-checks of Elon Musk's statements at the DealBook Summit show his timeline regarding the pre-invasion deployment of Starlink terminals in Ukraine is unsupported by the historical record.
Musk's claim that Russia disabled every other Ukrainian communications system is false, as alternative networks and systems remained operational despite severe disruptions.

Reports contradict Musk's suggestion that recent restrictions on military-grade Starshield services were solely the responsibility of the U.S. government, with investigations pointing to Musk himself.

source_summaries.title: One Illusion Is Dying, But There Is One More To Go
bullets: An ongoing illusion is dying in the US and Europe regarding Trump's absolute commitment to Russia and Vladimir Putin.
A more pernicious illusion persists that Donald Trump is genuinely anti-China and cares about United States national security.
Trump's primary priority in Asia has consistently been to cut lucrative deals with China while disregarding US allies and national interests.

source_summaries.title: The 2026 Postmortem: A Blowout, A Polling Miss, And The Road To 2028
bullets: Democrats secured majorities in the 2026 midterm elections, winning at least 258 House seats and 56 Senate seats.
Polls averaged a 9-point lead for Democrats on the generic ballot, while the party ultimately won the popular vote by 14 points.
Analysts discussed whether the election results stemmed from voter persuasion or turnout shifts, alongside implications for the 2028 presidential cycle.

source_summaries.title: No Consensus, No Surprise
bullets: COP31 concluded without an overarching deal after two weeks of negotiations due to a lack of consensus among participating nations.
A Saudi-led group opposed reaffirming the fossil fuel transition pledge from COP28, advocating instead for carbon capture technologies.
The IEA identified the Strait of Hormuz disruption as a major energy supply shock that could significantly impact future global oil and gas demand.

source_summaries.title: Response to Controversy
bullets: Sam Harris has published a fully updated version of his 2013 article addressing controversies surrounding his work on topics such as Trump, Covid, Islam, and free speech.
The author states that much of the controversy he faces stems from unscrupulous critics and out-of-context video clips deliberately misrepresenting his views.
Harris explains that defending against defamation is difficult because critics can easily spread smears while rebuttals often fail to reach the same audience.

source_summaries.title: The Newspapers Japan Couldn’t Ban
bullets: Exiled Japanese activists in the San Francisco Bay Area utilized American free speech protections to publish newspapers critical of Japan's Meiji government.
Publications such as Shin Nippon, Aikoku, Liberty, and The Nineteenth Century were smuggled back across the Pacific to sustain democratic resistance against censorship.
Activist Korei Ishizuka helped found Shin Nippon in Oakland after arriving in California, eventually transitioning from journalism to farming while remaining pursued by state power.

source_summaries.title: Jensen is Too Big to Fail
bullets: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO eleven days after his resignation following revelations regarding an affair with a Chinese spy.
Financial pressures and intervention from Donald Trump drove the board to reverse its decision, highlighting that the company and Huang were deemed too big to fail.
The author argues that the situation demonstrates how wealth, market dominance, and political connections can override national security and legal accountability.

source_summaries.title: 📈 Monday data: Turbulence is getting weirder, and nobody knows why
bullets: Clear-air turbulence conditions worldwide reached a 47-year high from August through October.
El Niño and long-term climate trends fail to fully account for this recent spike in atmospheric turbulence.
The majority of the unusual autumn turbulence distribution remains unexplained by current models.

source_summaries.title: Three Suspects — Why the Ukraine War Is Getting More Dangerous
bullets: Prof. Robert Pape argues that Russia has made minimal territorial gains in Ukraine through October, with current advancement rates indicating it would take decades or millennia to conquer the claimed regions.
Massive Russian troop casualties heavily exceed recruitment numbers, driven largely by an expansive drone-enforced kill zone that prevents traditional armor breakthroughs.
Blaming only Moscow, Trump, or Zelensky misses the broader strategic reality that Russia's military strategy is failing to achieve its territorial objectives.

source_summaries.title: What’s Missing in the Screens-in-Schools Debate
bullets: Current screens-in-schools debates often overlook the physical impact of how students use their hands during the school day.
Children are experiencing a crisis of deteriorating fine-motor skills, such as difficulties gripping crayons, using scissors, or buttoning coats.
Typing on a screen provides a sensorimotor shortcut that skips essential visuomotor, haptic, and cognitive steps involved in handwriting.
